longFormInfo: Alexandria became the administrative centre of Roman Egypt after Octavian defeated Cleopatra VII and Mark Antony in 30 BCE.
The city remained under Roman imperial rule until the administrative and political transition conventionally associated with the Byzantine period after the division of the Roman Empire in 395 CE.

longFormInfo: The year 395 CE is used as the conventional boundary between the Roman and Byzantine periods following the permanent division of the Roman Empire after the death of Theodosius I.
Roman administrative institutions and cultural influences continued beyond 395 CE, so the boundary is chronological and conventional rather than an abrupt local political rupture.

tradeAndCommerce: Exports included grain, papyrus, textiles, glass, Egyptian luxury goods and spices trans-shipped through the Red Sea.
Imports included wine, olive oil, timber, metals, manufactured goods and luxury products from the wider Mediterranean and Indian Ocean networks.
